claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure containing an fcc matrix and hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
Coexistence with the C14 Laves phase enhances the coercivity of FeCoNiTi.
The dual-phase alloy can reach approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K.
The Ti-rich C14 phase couples antiferromagnetically to the Fe-Co-Ni fcc phase.
Antiferromagnetic coupling occurs between Fe, Co, or Ni sublattices and Ti within the C14 phase.
The fcc/C14 interface introduces strain because of crystallographic mismatch.
Ti-induced electronic modifications at the fcc/C14 interface generate local magnetic anisotropy.
Antiferromagnetic coupling between Ti 3d states in C14 and Fe, Co, or Ni 3d states in fcc locally suppresses saturation magnetization.
The proposed interphase antiferromagnetic coupling generates strong local magnetic anisotropy.
The fcc/C14 phase boundaries physically pin magnetic domain walls.
Local anisotropy and domain-wall pinning impede domain reversal and thereby increase coercivity.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because their orbital moments are insufficient.
The absence of phase-boundary pinning contributes to the lower coercivity of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys.
Ferromagnetic ordering transitions occur near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K and influence the magnetic ground state.
Effective pinning may require the C14 volume fraction to exceed a percolation threshold.
A dual-phase, C14-rich FeCoNiTi alloy should be compared with a C14-suppressed fcc alloy using temperature-dependent magnetization and hysteresis measurements.
Spin-polarized density-of-states calculations should evaluate the spin-resolved DOS at the Fermi level for the fcc and C14 phases.
The hypothesis is falsified if the dual-phase alloy has no significant coercivity increase over the C14-suppressed fcc control at 400 K.
The hypothesis is falsified if the fcc phase's spin DOS at the Fermi level is not modified by proximity to C14.

contradictions.description: The coupling is described inconsistently as interphase coupling between Ti-rich C14 and Fe-Co-Ni fcc, as coupling among sublattices within C14, and as direct coupling between C14 Ti states and fcc transition-metal states.
